raw_response:
I farm 8 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will use the same 8 mu for both crops across the year. Because I have 25 years of experience and some of my family work off-farm, I will keep my plan practical and not too labor-heavy. I have well irrigation, so I will rely on stable water at the key stages instead of gambling on rainfall. For wheat, I will use improved seed, put enough nitrogen to push tillering and grain filling, and give moderate phosphorus and potassium to hold yield steady. I will use rotary tillage because it fits my usual way of preparing land after maize and keeps the field workable. For maize, I will plant hybrid seed because I care most about stable output, and I will use no-tillage after wheat harvest to save time, keep moisture, and reduce labor pressure during the busy summer changeover. I will not overdo pesticide sprays, but I will spray when I think weeds, insects, or disease could reduce yield. My goal is steady production from both crops, not chasing the highest possible yield with the highest possible cost.
